connection: Session 11 named ClockEntryRepository's public _clockEntries field as a real, unfixed encapsulation gap and promised to revisit it here. This session fixes it, and studies Timesheet -- a new extension composing Employee and List<ClockEntry> -- as a contrast in deliberate composition.
objectives: Fix ClockEntryRepository's real public _clockEntries field: make it private, and confirm every existing caller still compiles using only SaveClockEntry/GetClockEntry/GetEmployeeClockEntries.
Contrast that fix with ClockEntry's own ClockOut property, which was already correctly encapsulated (get with a private set) from the very first session.
Read Timesheet as composition: it owns an Employee and a List<ClockEntry>, and enforces (via Add) that every ClockEntry actually belongs to its Employee.
Explain why Timesheet.Add throws rather than silently ignoring a mismatched EmployeeId.

visuals.title: Before: any caller could bypass SaveClockEntry
visuals.explanation: public readonly List<ClockEntry> _clockEntries let external code call repository._clockEntries.Clear() directly -- a real gap identified in Session 11.

visuals.title: After: only the repository's own methods can touch storage
visuals.explanation: Making _clockEntries private forces every interaction through SaveClockEntry, GetClockEntry, and GetEmployeeClockEntries -- exactly the surface IClockEntryRepository already promises.

visuals.title: ClockEntry.ClockOut was already encapsulated correctly
visuals.explanation: public DateTime? ClockOut { get; private set; } has been this way since Session 6 -- only ClockOutEmployee can change it, which is why Session 17 is a repository fix, not a ClockEntry fix.

visuals.title: Timesheet composes an Employee and a List<ClockEntry>
visuals.explanation: Timesheet does not inherit from either type -- it owns one Employee and a private list of that employee's ClockEntry objects, exposed only as IReadOnlyList<ClockEntry>.

preQuiz.prompt: What real, external capability does making ClockEntryRepository's _clockEntries field private remove?
options: Direct access to _clockEntries.Clear(), .Add(...), or indexing from any code outside ClockEntryRepository -- the exact bypass Session 11 identified as a real, unfixed gap
preQuiz.explanation: This is precisely the fix Session 11 promised: private forces every interaction through the repository's own three methods, closing the bypass without changing any of IClockEntryRepository's public contract.

preQuiz.prompt: Why was ClockEntry.ClockOut never a similar problem, even though it is also a mutable piece of state?
options: ClockOut has always had a private setter (public DateTime? ClockOut { get; private set; }) -- only ClockOutEmployee, a method on ClockEntry itself, can ever change it; there was never a public-field-style bypass to begin with
ClockOut is a value type and therefore automatically safe
ClockOut is read-only and can never change
preQuiz.explanation: This is a genuinely different situation from _clockEntries -- ClockEntry got its encapsulation right from Session 6; the repository's field is what needed the fix.

preQuiz.prompt: Why does Timesheet.Add throw ArgumentException when given a ClockEntry whose EmployeeId doesn't match the Timesheet's own Employee?
options: A Timesheet's whole reason for existing is grouping one employee's entries together -- silently accepting a mismatched entry would corrupt that invariant without any visible sign of the mistake
ArgumentException is required by every Add method in C#
It has no real reason -- it is arbitrary
preQuiz.explanation: This mirrors Session 24's throw-vs-return rule: adding another employee's entry to this Timesheet is a broken caller expectation, not an expected everyday outcome, so it throws rather than silently ignoring the mismatch.

concept.title: Fixing the real encapsulation gap
paragraphs: The fix is one word: public readonly List<ClockEntry> _clockEntries becomes private readonly List<ClockEntry> _clockEntries. Every existing real method (SaveClockEntry, GetClockEntry, GetEmployeeClockEntries) is a member of the same class, so none of them need to change.

Every caller outside ClockEntryRepository -- ClockEntryService, PayrollService, every test -- was already going through the interface's three methods, never the field directly, so this fix is observable only in that the old bypass (repository._clockEntries.Clear()) now fails to compile.

concept.title: Contrast: ClockEntry.ClockOut was correct from the start
paragraphs: ClockEntry's constructor and ClockOutEmployee have not changed since Session 6 -- ClockOut's private setter already prevented exactly the kind of external bypass _clockEntries just had.
Seeing both the correct original design (ClockEntry) and the real gap that needed fixing (ClockEntryRepository) side by side is what makes 'encapsulation' concrete instead of abstract.
concept.code: public DateTime? ClockOut { get; private set; }   // correct since Session 6 -- never needed fixing

concept.title: Timesheet: composition with an enforced invariant
paragraphs: Timesheet owns an Employee (assigned once, in its constructor) and a private List<ClockEntry> exposed only as IReadOnlyList<ClockEntry> -- callers can read Entries but cannot Add to it directly; they must go through Timesheet.Add.
Add's real check -- entry.EmployeeId != Employee.EmployeeId -- is what keeps every entry in Entries genuinely belonging to this Timesheet's Employee, for the lifetime of the object.

lab.objective: Make ClockEntryRepository's _clockEntries field private, confirm the whole solution still builds, and exercise Timesheet's composition invariant.
lab.startingCondition: ClockEntryRepository's _clockEntries field is still public, as in the real source repository; Timesheet already exists with its real composition and Add invariant.
steps: Change _clockEntries from public to private in ClockEntryRepository.cs.
Build the whole solution and confirm nothing outside ClockEntryRepository referenced the field directly (it should not have).
Write a Timesheet, add one matching ClockEntry successfully, then attempt to add a ClockEntry with a different EmployeeId and confirm ArgumentException is thrown.
Confirm Timesheet.Entries is read-only from the outside -- Entries.Add(...) should not compile.
lab.expectedBehavior: The solution builds and all tests pass after the private-field fix; Timesheet.Add succeeds for a matching entry and throws for a mismatched one; Entries cannot be mutated directly from outside Timesheet.
lab.validation: dotnet build TimeClock.sln --configuration Release && dotnet test TimeClock.sln --configuration Release

expectedFiles.why: Change _clockEntries from public to private, closing the real encapsulation gap named in Session 11.
Confirm the real composition and EmployeeId-matching invariant.
Confirm both the successful-add and mismatched-employee-throws cases.
Publish synchronized lesson, lab, and quiz material.

review: The _clockEntries field is private, and every existing real method still compiles unchanged.
No caller outside ClockEntryRepository referenced the field directly before or after the fix.
ClockEntry.ClockOut's already-correct encapsulation is used as a contrast, not silently ignored.
Timesheet's Add invariant is demonstrated with both a passing and a throwing case.

postQuiz.prompt: Why did fixing _clockEntries's visibility require no changes to IClockEntryRepository or any of its three method signatures?
options: The interface never exposed the field in the first place -- SaveClockEntry, GetClockEntry, and GetEmployeeClockEntries were always the intended public surface; only the field's accidental public visibility needed correcting
IClockEntryRepository was also changed as part of the fix
It required changes to every class implementing IClockEntryRepository
postQuiz.explanation: This is exactly why the fix is small and safe -- the intended contract (the interface) was already correct; only an implementation detail (the field's visibility) needed to catch up to it.

postQuiz.prompt: Could Timesheet have used inheritance (Timesheet : Employee) instead of composition (Timesheet owning an Employee) to associate an employee with their entries?
options: No -- a Timesheet is not a kind of Employee (inheritance's 'is-a' relationship doesn't hold); it HAS an Employee, which is exactly what composition ('has-a') models
Yes -- inheritance and composition are interchangeable here
Only if Employee were declared abstract
postQuiz.explanation: This is the classic is-a versus has-a distinction: Timesheet has an Employee and a list of that employee's entries -- it is not itself a more specific kind of Employee.

postQuiz.prompt: What would happen if Timesheet.Entries returned List<ClockEntry> instead of IReadOnlyList<ClockEntry>?
options: Callers could call Entries.Add(...) or Entries.Clear() directly, bypassing Timesheet.Add's EmployeeId-matching check entirely -- reintroducing the exact kind of bypass Session 17 just fixed in ClockEntryRepository
Nothing would change -- List<T> and IReadOnlyList<T> expose identical members
The code would fail to compile
postQuiz.explanation: IReadOnlyList<T> deliberately omits Add/Remove/Clear -- returning the narrower interface is what protects Timesheet's own invariant, the same principle Session 13 covered for GetEmployeeClockEntries.

reflections: Why did this exact same kind of bug (a public field bypassing intended validation) not exist anywhere in ClockEntry itself?
What would you check for, in a code review, to catch a class exposing a mutable field the way ClockEntryRepository originally did?
How does Timesheet's IReadOnlyList<ClockEntry> return type connect back to Session 13's discussion of interface-level promises?
whatBreaks: Leaving _clockEntries public keeps the real bypass Session 11 identified: any code with a ClockEntryRepository reference can clear or directly mutate stored entries, invalidating anything SaveClockEntry might someday enforce. Changing Timesheet.Entries to return the mutable List<ClockEntry> directly would let callers add entries without EmployeeId validation, reintroducing the same class of bug in a different class.
summary: ClockEntryRepository's real public _clockEntries field -- named as a gap in Session 11 -- is fixed here by making it private, with no change required to IClockEntryRepository or any of its three real methods. ClockEntry.ClockOut's private setter shows what correct encapsulation looked like from the start. Timesheet demonstrates composition: it owns an Employee and a list of that employee's entries, and Add enforces that every entry actually belongs to it.
